agentCan: Sign the private_key_jwt client assertion and mint service-app tokens (client credentials)
Run the Authorization Code with PKCE flow for user-based access
Host a JWKS URL so Okta fetches keys dynamically (eases key rotation)

approval.cost: No submission or listing fee is stated in the OIN documentation read; submissions are made from the (free) Integrator Free Plan org, and no fee figure is published in the docs read
approval.trigger: Connecting to a customer org: no Okta vendor review. The approver is the customer org's administrator: only a Super Admin can grant Okta API scopes to an app ('Only the Super Admin role has permission to grant scopes to an app'), and an org admin must create the app integration, assign admin roles (service apps) or assign users/groups (OIDC apps). No Okta-side approval, certification, or fee is documented for creating app integrations in an org. OIN catalog listing: Okta vendor review REQUIRED. 'The OIN team verifies your submitted integration before they publish it in the OIN catalog.' The OIN Wizard 'is only available in Integrator Free Plan orgs', and the submitter must be 'an admin user in the Integrator Free Plan org with either the super admin or the app and org admin roles'. Account requirement: 'Submit your integration from an Okta account that has your company domain in the email address. You can't use an account with a personal email address. The OIN team doesn't review submissions from personal email accounts.' Testing artifacts: 'A dedicated test admin account in your app is required for Okta integration testing. This test account needs to be active during the submission review period', with privileges to configure admin settings and administer test users in your app; 'After your integration is verified, Okta automatically deletes test account credentials 30 days after your app is published'. Process: 'After you submit your integration, your integration is queued for OIN initial review. Okta sends you an email with the expected initial review completion date. The OIN review process consists of two phases: 1. The initial review phase 2. The QA testing phase. Okta sends you an email at each phase of the process to inform you of the status, the expected phase completion date, and any issues for you to fix.' Caps: 'You can have a maximum of 10 submissions for any Integrator Free Plan org in the OIN Manager', while 'The Integrator Free Plan org has no limit on active instances.' Updates: editing a published integration creates a new version that 'undergoes the same process flow as the original submission'; the update must be submitted from the same Integrator org used originally, 'otherwise, the Okta OIN team rejects the update'.
approval.wait: No fixed public timeline: Okta communicates an 'expected initial review completion date' and per-phase completion dates by email after submission; no number of days is stated in the guide

blockers.detail: 'The Okta org authorization server returns all scopes that you request... as long as the client app is permitted to use that scope (granted to the client app). It doesn't matter whether you have permissions for all the scopes that you request... However, when you make requests to perform actions that you don't have permissions for, the token doesn't work, and you receive an error.' For user-based tokens the effective privilege is min(app grants, authorizing user's admin role); for service apps, min(app grants, admin roles assigned to the app).
blockers.howToClear: Assign the app the admin roles matching its scopes during onboarding, and test real API calls, not just token contents.
blockers.title: Silent downscoping: grants are not permissions

blockers.detail: Custom authorization servers cannot mint access tokens containing Okta API scopes: integrations must target https://{org}/oauth2/v1/... (the org server), a common integration mistake. Scope-granting is Super-Admin-only, so onboarding a customer always requires their Super Admin's involvement at grant time.
blockers.howToClear: Hard-code the org authorization server for Okta API scopes and plan for a Super Admin session in onboarding.
blockers.title: Only the org authorization server works for Okta API scopes

blockers.detail: private_key_jwt is the only client authentication for service apps that want tokens with Okta scopes ('This is the only authentication method supported for OAuth 2.0 service apps'), and the private key is shown once: 'This is your only opportunity to save the private key.' Losing it means generating a new key pair in the customer org. A related footgun: if the customer org has 'Public client app admins' enabled, service apps are auto-assigned SUPER_ADMIN after scope grants; Okta advises disabling it after incorporating role assignments.
blockers.howToClear: Save the private key at generation (or register a JWKS URL for dynamic fetching) and have the customer check the Public client app admins setting.
blockers.title: Private key shown once; auto-super-admin footgun

OIDC app types for Okta-as-IdP use (Web Application / Single-Page App / Native App with Authorization Code, optionally PKCE, Refresh Token, Interaction Code grants): the same 'app integration' object with the opposite trust direction
flavor.recommended: Per customer org: an API Services (service) app with Client Credentials + private_key_jwt for machine-to-machine access; an OIDC Web Application (Authorization Code with PKCE) for user-based access
flavor.why: The object is an App Integration (Applications > Applications > Create App Integration in the Admin Console, or via the Apps API), identified by a Client ID (and Client Secret, or a public/private key pair). Two patterns must not be conflated: (a) a third-party SaaS connecting to a customer's Okta org (the SaaS's software calls the Okta APIs of each customer's org; there is no central multi-tenant client, the app integration is created inside each customer org by that org's admin, optionally distributed as a pre-configured template through the OIN catalog); and (b) Okta as your identity provider (an OIDC app in your own org so users sign in to your app with Okta). For (a) machine-to-machine: 'The Client Credentials grant flow is intended for server-side (confidential) client apps with no end user... To mint access tokens that contain Okta scopes, the Client Credentials flow is the only flow supported with an OAuth 2.0 service app', with private_key_jwt client authentication and admin roles assigned to the app for least privilege. For (a) user-based: 'Okta recommends that you always use the Authorization Code with PKCE grant flow', yielding 'an access token that is scoped for specific resources and actions and tied to the permissions of an Okta user'. Okta API scopes follow okta.<resource>.<operation> (e.g. okta.users.read, okta.users.manage; .self variants 'only allow access to the user who authorized the token'), and 'Only the org authorization server can mint access tokens that contain Okta API scopes'.

humanMust: (Customer org admin) Create the app integration in each customer org (API Services for M2M, or OIDC Web Application for user-based)
(Customer org admin) For service apps: configure Public key / Private key client authentication and generate the JWKS key pair ('This is your only opportunity to save the private key')
(Customer org Super Admin) Grant the Okta API scopes to the app in its Okta API Scopes tab
(Customer org admin) Assign admin roles to the service app (or assign users/groups to the OIDC app)
(Optional, for OIN listing) Build and test in an Okta Integrator Free Plan org and submit via the OIN Wizard with a dedicated test admin account
name: Okta
nuances: Token lifetimes (OIDC API reference): on the Okta Authorization Server they are hard-coded: 'ID token: 60 minutes; Access token: 60 minutes; Refresh token: 90 days'. On a Custom Authorization Server they are configurable via Access Policy (access tokens 5 minutes to 24 hours; refresh tokens with an idle window of at least 10 minutes and a maximum of five years; ID tokens fixed at 60 minutes). The client assertion JWT's exp must be 'a maximum of only an hour in the future'.

Refresh-token rotation is not a lifetime extension: 'when a new refresh token is returned, it inherits the maximum refresh token lifetime of the preceding refresh token', and an idle window also applies (the refresh token expires if the app fails to use it within the configured idle time). Long-lived offline access must be designed around the org's access policy.

Consent defaults differ by creation path: 'Apps created on /api/v1/apps default to consent_method=TRUSTED, while those created on /oauth2/v1/clients default to consent_method=REQUIRED', and 'If you request a scope that requires consent while using the client_credentials flow, an error is returned. Because there is no user, no consent can be given.' Custom scope names 'must not start with okta. or okta:'. App rate limits: 'By default, each new app sets this percentage at 50%' (Application rate limits tab).

OIN one-way doors: submissions from personal email accounts are not reviewed at all; updates submitted from a different Integrator org than the original are rejected; published-integration fixes go through the full two-phase review again. Choosing the wrong OIDC app type for public clients is a documented trap ('Choosing the wrong app type may result in Okta API endpoints attempting to verify an app's client secret').
prerequisites: A customer Okta org admin (Super Admin for scope grants) per customer
Secure storage for the service app's private key (shown once) or a hosted JWKS URL
For OIN listing: an Integrator Free Plan org and a company-domain email account

steps.detail: Admin Console > Applications > Create App Integration > API Services. Configure client authentication as Public key / Private key; 'leave the default of Save keys in Okta, and then click Add key... Click Generate new key' and save the private key immediately (your only opportunity). Alternatively register a JWKS URL the vendor hosts.

links.label: Implement OAuth for Okta with a service app

steps.title: (Service app) Create the API Services app; generate the key pair

steps.detail: In the app's Okta API Scopes tab, click Grant for each required scope (okta.<resource>.<operation>). 'Only the Super Admin role has permission to grant scopes to an app.' Then assign admin roles to the service app to constrain its permissions ('For each service app you create, you need to assign admin roles to constrain the permissions and resources of that app for least privilege access').

links.label: Set up Okta for OAuth API access

steps.title: (Super Admin) Grant scopes; assign admin roles

steps.detail: Sign a JWT client assertion (aud = https://{yourOktaDomain}/oauth2/v1/token, iss = the service app's Client ID, exp at most one hour ahead) with the private key and POST it to the org's /oauth2/v1/token with grant_type=client_credentials and the requested scopes. Call the Okta APIs with the resulting Bearer token (lifetime fixed at one hour on the org server).
steps.title: Mint tokens (client credentials + private_key_jwt)

steps.detail: Create App Integration > OIDC - OpenID Connect > Web Application (Authorization Code is required and 'can't clear the checkbox'); set Sign-in redirect URIs; assign users/groups (or 'Limit access to selected groups'); note the Client ID and Client secret. Grant Okta API scopes as above. Run Authorization Code with PKCE against the org authorization server (/oauth2/v1/authorize, exchange at /oauth2/v1/token); tokens last one hour.
steps.title: (User-based alternative) OIDC Web App + Auth Code with PKCE

steps.detail: Build and test the integration in an Okta Integrator Free Plan org (submitter: an admin with super admin or app/org admin role, using a company-domain email). Submit via the OIN Wizard with a dedicated test admin account (active during review). Review runs two phases (initial review, QA testing) with expected completion dates emailed per phase. After publication, 'Okta automatically deletes test account credentials 30 days after your app is published'. Maximum 10 submissions per Integrator Free Plan org.

tagline: Self-serve per customer org, with two traps: a token can carry scopes the app has no permission to use (grants are not permissions), and only the org authorization server can mint Okta API scopes. The reviewed path is only the optional OIN catalog listing.
